content:
incident-bot: 🚨 *INC-2025-03-05-042* opened by @Rafael Mendes
Severity: SEV-2
Service: Hosted Inference API
Suspected region: us-east-1
Symptom: elevated 5xx + timeouts
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/eng-sre/runbooks/region-degradation

Rafael Mendes: seeing a spike on hosted chat completions in us-east-1. 5xx jumped from ~0.3% to ~6-8% over last 10m, p99 latency also bad.
Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/hosted-api?var-region=us-east-1
Can someone from routing + infra hop in?

Sean Gallagher: here. assign IC to @Rafael Mendes. I’ll be backup IC.
First step: confirm scope (hosted vs dedicated), and whether this is partial impairment vs full outage. Also check upstream deps (auth, policy store, edge).

Aisha Bello: pulling SLO burn view now. Multi-region availability burn is at ~12x for hosted in us-east-1 route group.
Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/slo-burn?var-slo=hosted-mr-availability&var-region=us-east-1
We’re going to page if it sustains >5m.

Miles Thornton: looking at request traces. pattern: retries + connect timeouts to gpu-gateway in us-east-1, not model failures.
Do we have any packet loss alarms from edge -> fleet?

Victor Alvarez: checking edge health. seeing elevated TCP retransmits on one path (iad edge POP -> us-east-1a). Not across the board.
Also seeing BGP flap around 03:58-04:03 UTC.

Irene Choi: fleet side: gpu pool headroom is *fine* (util ~62%) but queue depth is climbing in one AZ (use1a). could be network partition-ish.
We can try draining that AZ / shifting traffic to use1b/use1c.

Mina Haddad: routing policy currently sticky by region then AZ preference (use1a is first for some shards).
We can hotpatch policy to de-prefer use1a for hosted routes. That’s manual right now.

Vikram Singh: +1. I can do policy change via admin endpoint (no deploy), but we need sign-off: it can increase p99 slightly due to cross-AZ hops.

Rafael Mendes: ok, priority is stop the 5xx/timeouts.
Action proposal:
1) de-prefer use1a for hosted inference (chat + completions)
2) if still bad, consider partial failover of hosted traffic to us-west-2
Question: how safe is us-west-2 capacity right now?

Harish Reddy: checking west. us-west-2 headroom is ~18% on A100 pool, ~22% on H100 pool. If we swing a big chunk suddenly, risk queueing.
If we do it, do canary 5% then 15% then 30%.
Dedicated is tight in west (a couple reserved customers), so keep it hosted-only unless we’re desperate.

Dev Patel: Support is getting pings already (2 tickets in last 5m, mostly streaming disconnects + retries). Please keep me posted on customer-visible behavior.

Tomáš Novák: per runbook, first mitigation for partial impairment is *in-region* reroute (AZ drain) + tighten timeouts, then cross-region failover only if error budget burn stays >10x.
But we’ve been slow in past incidents deciding when to do cross-region. Let’s timebox.

Aisha Bello: if this continues >10m at current rate, we’ll eat ~20-25% of weekly budget for hosted MR availability.
Would prefer quick mitigation even if p99 increases a bit.

Mina Haddad: I can update routing policy weights now:
- hosted/chat: use1a weight from 0.45 -> 0.05
- hosted/completions: use1a weight from 0.40 -> 0.05
Leave embeddings alone for now.
Needs @Vikram Singh to apply.

Vikram Singh: ready. can someone confirm there’s no ongoing deploy that will stomp policy?

deploy-bot: No active production deploys for `routing-policy-service`.
Last deploy: `routing-policy-service` 2025.03.04.19 at 02:11 UTC (green)

Rafael Mendes: go ahead.

Vikram Singh: applying policy patch…
Command used:
`policyctl apply --env prod --region us-east-1 --file /tmp/use1a-deprefer-hosted.yaml`
Audit link: https://console.redwood/audit/policy/evt_7f3c2

Miles Thornton: watching live metrics. 5xx dropping slightly but timeouts still high.
Still seeing connect timeouts to gateway in use1a (maybe residual sessions?)

Victor Alvarez: edge path issue still present. packet loss on one route is ~2-3%, which is enough to kill streaming.
We can force edge to prefer alternate POP? That’s more invasive.

Irene Choi: if it’s localized to use1a, draining should help. But we also have long-lived connections pinned.
We can force gateway to close conns in use1a (rolling restart) to flush.
Risk: brief spike.

Sean Gallagher: do it but stagger. keep hosted only. we need to avoid making it worse.

Irene Choi: starting rolling restart of `gpu-gateway` in use1a only.

statuspage-bot: Drafted internal status update (not published):
“Investigating elevated error rates and latency impacting Hosted Inference API in us-east-1. Mitigations in progress.”

Rafael Mendes: hold on status page for now, want to see if mitigation works in next 5m.

Aisha Bello: alert just fired (burn-rate > 10x over 5m). Paging policy says SEV-2 page is ok; already in channel.

Tomáš Novák: if errors don’t recover in next 5-7m, we should do progressive failover. Otherwise we’ll keep debating.
This is exactly the decision point we keep missing automation for.

Miles Thornton: restart seems to help. connect timeouts down, but still above normal.
Current: 5xx ~2.1% (down from 7-8%), p99 ~4.8s (baseline 1.2s).

Harish Reddy: if we failover even 10-15% hosted to west, we can absorb, but please avoid 50%+.
Also check west auth + rate limiters; we’ve seen them become bottlenecks on sudden shifts.

Mina Haddad: we can do progressive failover manually by setting routing policy override for hosted tier.
It’s annoying because it’s not a single knob; have to adjust per route group.

Rafael Mendes: ok. decision:
- If in-region mitigation doesn’t get 5xx <1% in next 5m, we do hosted-only 10% shift to us-west-2.
- Dedicated stays pinned.
Everyone ok?

Sean Gallagher: 👍

Aisha Bello: 👍

Dev Patel: 👍 (please tell Support what customers may see if west shift happens—higher latency but fewer errors?)

Rafael Mendes: yep. we’ll message: “may see slightly higher latency; errors should reduce.”

Irene Choi: rolling restart completed for use1a. queue depth now normalizing.

Miles Thornton: metrics now: 5xx 0.9-1.1% (hovering), timeouts still elevated but trending down.
p99 3.2s.

Victor Alvarez: network looks better too. retransmits down. whatever was flapping seems to have stabilized.

Tomáš Novák: if it’s stabilizing, maybe hold off on cross-region shift. But keep ready.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. we’ll monitor 10m.

Aisha Bello: SLO burn rate down to ~3x now. still not great but not emergency.

Dev Patel: Support update: I’ll tell them mitigation ongoing; expect recovery. No need for customer broadcast yet.

Mina Haddad: note for follow-up: we spent ~20m deciding and doing manual steps (policy edits + fleet drain). If the signals had been aggregated + a safe-to-failover check existed, this would’ve been near-instant.

Miles Thornton: +1. also, we had to rely on humans to infer “partial impairment” vs “full region” and pick the right lever (AZ drain vs failover).
We should codify:
- trigger on connect timeout + tail latency + gateway error rate
- require west capacity + auth health checks before shifting traffic
- add hysteresis/hold-down so we don’t flap

Sean Gallagher: capture action items:
1) add clear region health signals for network path + gateway connect errors
2) define thresholds + windows
3) progressive failover automation with safe checks
This thread is basically the justification doc.

Rafael Mendes: incident status: *mitigated*. errors down to ~0.6%, p99 2.0s and falling.
Let’s keep channel open 30m.

statuspage-bot: Internal status draft updated (not published):
“Mitigation applied; monitoring recovery. Some requests may have seen elevated latency/timeouts.”

Tomáš Novák: for the retro: we should note we had no single dashboard showing “safe to failover?” (capacity headroom + dependency health). we asked Harish manually.

Harish Reddy: yep. capacity signals exist but not wired into routing decisions.

Mina Haddad: also: manual policy patch is risky—no guardrails, no automatic rollback. We were lucky no deploy stomped it.

Aisha Bello: recovery check at +25m: 5xx 0.25%, p99 1.4s. burn-rate back to ~1.1x.

Rafael Mendes: closing incident as resolved. thanks all.
Next steps: I’ll file a retro + link this thread, and we’ll fold into the regional failover automation upgrade initiative.

incident-bot: ✅ *INC-2025-03-05-042 resolved* by @Rafael Mendes
Duration: 0:52:56
Customer impact: Elevated errors/timeouts for Hosted Inference API in us-east-1 (partial), no full region failover executed
Mitigations: AZ de-preference (routing), gateway restart/drain in use1a, monitoring + SLO burn reduction
Retro: pending
